key_drivers: Q1 FY27 EPS guide $1.38-1.40 sits exactly on the $1.38 consensus, and this management has been setting beatable bars
Last print (4 Jun 2026, FQ4) beat and the stock gapped ~6% higher, so the free rule (repeat last reaction sign) points up
Stock at $90.95, near the top of its 3-month range ($73.75-$94.13) and +23% over that window - the bar has already been raised
First quarter reported after the MiniMed separation: restated segments, stranded costs and royalty flows widen the dispersion of outcomes
Sell-side positioned for a beat-and-raise (Needham PT to $114); average PT ~$98 leaves room but not much cushion
what_would_change_my_mind: A guidance cut or an unfavourable restatement of the post-MiniMed cost base that makes the $5.90-6.00 FY27 EPS bridge look unreachable.
reasoning: The clean part of this setup is that Medtronic guided Q1 FY27 EPS to $1.38-1.40 and consensus settled at $1.38 - a bar the company set for itself and has recently cleared, with June's FQ4 beat producing a ~6% gap up. Base rates are unhelpful on their own: roughly a coin flip on direction over five years, median +2.5% up / -3.8% down, implied moves 3.0-4.1% with realised frequently larger (8.8% in Nov 2025). What tilts me up rather than neutral is the combination of a self-set bar, a positive last reaction, and a sell-side lined up for a raise. What holds the conviction to Low is the 23% three-month run into the print - the same beat that was worth +6% at $78 is worth less at $91 - and the reporting noise from the first post-MiniMed quarter, which cuts both ways. Size: 4.0%, above the 3-4% implied band because the separation makes the first restated print messier than a normal Medtronic quarter. Prices as of 2026-08-31 ~17:40 UTC. Research, not advice.

key_drivers: Last quarter NIO beat EPS outright ($0.02 vs -$0.34 expected) and the stock still fell ~7% - operational beats have stopped being rewarded
Q2 deliveries of 107,658 are already public and missed the company's own 110,000-115,000 guide, so the upside surprise has to come from margin, not volume
Fourth consecutive monthly decline; stock at $4.32, sitting on the low of its 3-month range ($4.32-$6.01)
Vehicle margin expected to step down to 17-18% from Q1's 18.8%, against a full-year 17-18% target that leaves no slack
Q3 guidance and cash burn are the swing factors, and this management has a history of guiding below hope
what_would_change_my_mind: A Q2 vehicle margin printing above 19% together with a Q3 delivery guide that credibly extends the +71% YoY July run-rate.
reasoning: The informative fact is May 21: NIO beat EPS by a wide margin, revenue landed in line, and the stock fell ~7% anyway. That is a market that has stopped paying for operational progress and is pricing margin durability and cash. Nothing since has changed that - deliveries missed the company's own Q2 guide, the shares have declined four months running and now sit on their three-month low, and vehicle margin is guided down sequentially. The bull case is entirely positioning: Stocktwits sentiment at 27/100, near a record low, in a name where revenue is nearly doubling. But washed-out sentiment has been true for months while the stock kept falling, and I do not think one quarter reverses it when the volume surprise is already banked and negative. Options imply about 9%; I take that as fair, since the last reaction was ~7% and this print carries both Q2 results and Q3 guidance. Scaled to 14.4% under the backtest's correction. Prices as of 2026-08-31 ~17:40 UTC. Research, not advice.

key_drivers: Only the second report as a standalone company (first was FQ4 in early June), so there is almost no reaction history to anchor on
Stock at $19.88, near its 3-month high of $20.70 and up ~66% from the $12.00 low - a high bar into the print
FY27 guided at ~10% organic growth with adj. EBITDA margin ~16%, a step down from FQ4's 18.4% - the margin line is where the disappointment would come from
Consensus $0.09 EPS on ~$828M revenue, versus $0.35 a year ago; the standalone cost structure makes YoY comparisons close to meaningless
Launch-dependent story (MiniMed Flex, Go, Instinct, Simplera) in a sector with well-resourced competitors
what_would_change_my_mind: Either an organic growth print clearly above the ~10% FY guide, or a margin miss that shows standalone costs running ahead of the 16% EBITDA plan.
reasoning: I can see why this could go either way and I cannot pick. Momentum is emphatically positive - up ~66% from the post-separation low, sitting near its high, with BofA lifting its target to $24 - and the FY26 exit was strong (FQ4 organic +8.7%, adj. EBITDA +32%). Against that, a stock that has already re-rated 66% needs a beat to hold, and the one number most likely to disappoint is exactly the one guided lower: EBITDA margin stepping to ~16% from 18.4% as standalone costs land. A newly separated company's second print is where those costs first become visible without a parent to absorb them. Neither side is strong enough to call, so I abstain. On size I am confident the move is large: a young spinoff, thin coverage, a stock at highs, and no established reaction pattern to damp it. 8.0% honest, 12.8% scaled. Prices as of 2026-08-31 ~17:40 UTC. Research, not advice.

key_drivers: H1 2026 revenue was pre-announced on 6 August at ~$127M against $6.32M a year earlier, so the headline is already out and the print is about the quality behind it
FuzzyPanda alleged in March 2026 that the company overstates both its AI technology and its financials - the H1 statements are where receivables and cash conversion get tested
Stock at $2.90 is mid-range ($2.24-$3.15), not near highs: the market has priced disbelief in the ramp rather than the ramp itself
August news flow was genuinely positive - Google Cloud deploying its database technology for Web3 indexing (+~21% on the week) and a Tech Mahindra partnership
High double-digit short interest plus a shareholder-approved buyback authority of up to $300M is a live squeeze configuration
what_would_change_my_mind: The cash flow statement: H1 operating cash conversion and the receivables balance behind that $127M either corroborate the revenue or do not, and one glance settles the direction.
reasoning: My first instinct was Lean Down on asymmetry: the good news (revenue) is already announced, while the untested item - whether $127M of revenue converted to cash - only has downside disclosure risk. I talked myself out of it. If that revenue claim were being believed, the stock would not be at $2.90 in the middle of its range with heavy short interest after pre-announcing a 20x revenue increase. What is priced here is scepticism, which means corroboration is a positive surprise and the asymmetry is roughly symmetric. Two loud, opposite outcomes sit on this print and I have no basis for picking between them, so I abstain rather than dress up a coin flip. Size is the part I am willing to commit to: a heavily shorted micro-to-small cap with a live fraud allegation reporting the statements that test it moves violently in either direction. 16% honest, 32% under the scaling rule - which I note is an aggressive number and is exactly the sort of case that will tell us whether the correction generalises. Prices as of 2026-08-31 ~17:40 UTC. Research, not advice.

key_drivers: Stock at $6.75, up ~78% from the $3.78 three-month low and near the $6.91 high, on an AI-search-visibility narrative (Scout MCP/API launch) rather than on reported growth
The underlying numbers are flat: Q1 FY27 revenue -1% YoY, ARR $440.8M, net retention 97% - ARR does not inflect in one quarter
Q1 FY27 beat guidance and the stock still fell ~9.5% that week; a beat is not sufficient at this price
Consensus price target had been cut to $5.67 and FY27 revenue forecasts to $443.6M, both below where the stock now trades
No live take-private: Walrath withdrew the $9.00 proposal on 2 February 2026 for lack of financing, replaced by a $150M self-tender - so there is no deal floor under the print
what_would_change_my_mind: Sequential ARR growth accelerating with Scout contributing disclosed bookings - that would make the re-rating a numbers story rather than a narrative one.
reasoning: A company growing revenue at -1% has nearly doubled in ten weeks because it launched an API into the AI-search theme and published a citation study. The print is where the narrative meets the ARR line, and ARR is a slow-moving quantity: $440.8M with 97% net retention does not turn in a quarter. The precedent is one report old - Q1 FY27 beat its own guidance and the shares fell ~9.5% in the following week, at a price less than half of today's. Buybacks and a reduced short base support the stock and are the main reason I keep this at Lean rather than Strong, along with the possibility that Scout bookings are real and disclosed. But there is no takeover bid underneath it any more: that proposal was withdrawn in February when financing failed. Size: YEXT moved ~9.5% off a smaller base and realised volatility is far higher after the run, so 12% honest, 24% scaled. Prices as of 2026-08-31 ~17:40 UTC. Research, not advice.
